claim: Simon's definition: bounded rationality = search plus satisficing (stop at first option meeting an aspiration level); aspirations adapt to the environment. A verbal theory with no experiment in the founding text.
agent_test: Compare a fixed-aspiration stop rule with an adaptive-aspiration rule (raise after easy wins, lower after failures) at equal tokens.

claim: Pure threshold satisficing is not what people do in short timed choice: stop probability rises smoothly (never above about 50% per fixation) and a hybrid of optimal search and random stopping fits best.
agent_test: Test hard-threshold stop vs soft (probabilistic, value-weighted) stop in the candidate-generation loop.

claim: Within what they have seen, people choose well (best seen item chosen 76%/73%/69% for 4/9/16 items) but what gets seen is driven by screen position, not value. Search coverage, not selection, is the weak step.
agent_test: Randomise the order candidates are shown to the agent selector and measure how much a first-listed bias costs.

claim: Take The Best (stop at first discriminating cue) matches regression on German city size (.658 vs .657 in simulation; out-of-sample 72.2 vs 71.9 from a Wikipedia secondary, original not opened) with far fewer lookups. Margin is tiny and domain-specific.
agent_test: Run stop-at-first-discriminating-check vs check-everything on a verification step; compare accuracy and tokens.

claim: Reasoning models fail to satisfice on easy tasks: o1-like models use 1,953% more tokens than conventional models on '2+3', the first solution round is already correct in over 92% of cases and uses under 60% of tokens. All numbers come from one paper (Chen et al.), re-opened and confirmed; a survey frames the same problem. Gap search 2026-11: other groups find the same pattern off the competition-math set. Answer convergence is near step 0 on NaturalQuestions and about 0.8 to 0.9 of the chain on GSM8K/MATH/GPQA/AIME (Liu and Wang 2025). Confidence-based exit keeps pass@1 on HumanEval, BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench with 34 to 80% of the tokens (DEER). The exact "first solution right in over 92%" figure is still one paper (Chen) and was not reproduced on code or planning.
agent_test: Add a first-correct stop check that needs no label (consistency or verifier); measure token saving at equal accuracy.

claim: Training to stop at the first correct solution cuts tokens 22-48% on math with accuracy roughly kept; on hard sets first-correct-only loses accuracy and one reflection round restores most of it. The 48.6% headline is a Fig. 1 number; Table 4 gives 44.7% (2407.9 to 1330.7 tokens) for MATH500.
agent_test: Gate by difficulty: stop early on easy items, allow one verify round on hard ones; compare against a fixed budget.

claim: Adaptive stopping rules in test-time compute cut samples or length with small accuracy cost: Adaptive-Consistency up to 7.9x fewer samples at under 0.1% average accuracy loss (re-opened, confirmed); early exit 19.1-80.1% shorter chains with +0.3 to +5.0% accuracy (abstract only). Gap search: DeepConf (consensus 0.95, K=512) cuts tokens 18 to 85% vs majority voting with accuracy mostly kept (4 math sets, 3 models); ESC cuts samples 34 to 84%. Caveat: baselines are fixed-budget, not equal-token; 42.4% (confidence) and 54.8% (consistency) of stop failures are premature (PUMA 2026). Samples from one model are correlated (G4) and no paper measured stop-signal calibration under that correlation.
agent_test: Replace fixed N-sample voting with Beta-test stopping; check saving and whether agreement among same-model samples misleads (G4).

claim: Allocating test-time compute by prompt difficulty beats uniform spending (about 4x less compute than best-of-N at matched performance; smaller model plus compute can beat a 14x larger one in some regimes). Needs a difficulty estimate. Gap search: Damani 2024 learns the difficulty predictor from hidden states: up to 50% less compute at equal reward on Math and Code, predictor ranking accuracy 72 to 84%, but 50% of Code problems have zero success, which a wrong probe over-funds. Prompt-only difficulty gating before any reasoning is unreliable (Zero-Step Thinking, best ROC-AUC 72.2, not stable across models).
agent_test: Implement a cheap difficulty probe at S0 and route to 1, 3 or 8 passes; equal-total-token comparison to fixed 3 passes.

claim: More samples raise coverage (15.9% to 56% on SWE-bench Lite at 250 samples, confirmed) but selection without a verifier plateaus, so a stop rule needs a verifier, not just a count.
agent_test: Compare stop-on-verifier-pass with stop-on-N-samples for coding items.

claim: Refinement with self-feedback gives about 20% absolute average gain but returns shrink by the third pass; feedback from the same model is weak evidence.
agent_test: Cap refine at 2 passes and compare with 4 passes at equal tokens.

claim: Searching with a rate-and-prune filter beats plain sampling at similar scale: Game of 24, GPT-4, ToT b=5 74% vs CoT best-of-100 49% (re-opened, confirmed). Compute per method differs.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of pruned tree search vs independent samples on a puzzle set.

claim: Satisficing alignment at inference: maximise one objective subject to thresholds on others gives +22.3% helpfulness win-tie vs a multi-objective decoder (confirmed in text), GPT-4 judged, 7B models; effect-size unit unclear, no best-of-N baseline. Gap search: re-read confirms the experiments use GPT-4 win-tie only, with decoding baselines, no human judges and no best-of-N arm at equal samples. Gap 10 stays open.
agent_test: Apply threshold-constrained selection (primary objective plus safety/format floors) vs weighted-sum selection.

claim: Current LLMs behave as near-perfect optimisers on numeric choice: no GARP violation in 81-95 of 100 runs, mean CCEI .997-.999 vs humans .963-.985; with CoT, models correlate .93-.94 with expected value vs humans .48. Zero-shot the same models are far less rational (.41 and .28). Consistency is not optimality; framing and temperature matter.
agent_test: Do not assume the agent needs de-biasing on numeric choice; test whether CoT moves answers toward ground truth, not toward human choice.

claim: Older or smaller models show human-like heuristic errors (GPT-3 fails all 3 CRT items intuitively; 70-90% intuitive wrong answers) that largely vanish in ChatGPT-4 (96% correct, 0% intuitive).
agent_test: Do not generalise 2022-23 bias findings to current models; re-run on the model we use.

claim: Deliberation can hurt: CoT lowers accuracy on tasks where verbal thinking hurts humans (up to 36.3 points), but not for every model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet no significant drop).
agent_test: Add a no-deliberation arm for tasks flagged intuitive and compare against forced CoT.

claim: Choice overload is conditional, not universal: a meta-analysis found a mean effect virtually zero over 63 conditions (50 experiments, 5,036 participants; abstract only) with moderators (set complexity, task difficulty, preference uncertainty, goal). The 24-vs-6 jam result (3% vs 30% purchase) is second-hand here. Gap search: Scheibehenne 2010 opened. Mean D = 0.02 (95% CI about -0.09 to 0.12, minus signs inferred), tau-squared 0.12, I-squared 68%; after 20% trimming D = 0.001. Expertise or prior preferences protects (b=.50); no linear effect of large-set size. Chernev 2015 (99 observations, N=7,202; abstract only) reports a significant overall effect once four moderators are included. No numeric overall d for Chernev was obtained.
agent_test: Vary number of candidate options shown to the agent selector (3, 6, 12, 24) and plot accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Making selection easier speeds choice but does not improve quality as sets grow; people save effort rather than reinvest it (N=17 and 28).
agent_test: Check whether a pre-filter that makes selection easier simply lowers selection effort in the agent.

claim: Maximizing self-report links to regret and lower satisfaction (regret r about .45-.5; life satisfaction r=-.24) but time-lagged work finds small positive effects on adjustment (beta .11-.17). The '20% higher salary' result is unverified (memory and second-hand only). Measurement is fragmented (up to 13 scales).
agent_test: Low relevance for the agent; trait scales do not map to an agent policy.

claim: Maximizing correlates with decision difficulty (r=.249) and need for closure (r=.339) among 96 senior police officers; with OCD tendencies in two online samples. No outcome-quality measure.
agent_test: None direct.

claim: Satisficing under risk is usually dominated by optimising; under uncertainty empirically derived simple strategies can do well. Threshold bandit satisficing has finite cumulative satisficing regret in theory. Both sources only partly opened. Gap search: Artinger 2022 abstract confirms the risk-vs-uncertainty split but the post-print could not be read (403). No LLM task was found that tests it.
agent_test: Fixed-threshold stopping in an exploration task with a known threshold vs UCB-style continuing.

claim: Speed-accuracy arbitration (habit vs search by value of information against time cost) explains rising reaction time with option count and the shift to habit. Model paper, no LLM test.
agent_test: Estimate value of another pass from the agent's own consistency signal and stop when below token cost.

claim: Respondents use simplifying rules (attribute non-attendance, thresholds) that bias preference estimates if ignored; response-time data help identify which rule is used.
agent_test: Log the agent's stopping step and check whether stop type predicts error.

claim: Everyday low-stakes conversations favour satisficing and heuristics (955 Korean conversations, LLM-coded; abstract only).
agent_test: None direct.

claim: Reasoning LLMs may beat the classical satisficing planner LAMA on multi-goal planning (abstract only).
agent_test: Verify before use.

claim: A model fine-tuned on 10.7M human choices predicts held-out human behaviour better than cognitive models, while base chat models are more rational than humans; a human predictor is not an optimal agent.
agent_test: None direct.

claim: LLMs show order and label bias when choosing among candidates. Moving the gold answer to the last of 4 slots cost gpt-3.5-turbo 6.3 points on MMLU (67.2 to 60.9); llama-30B picked A 34.6% vs D 15.8% with gold balanced; with 20 documents accuracy fell by over 20% in the worst gold position; judge position bias is largest when candidates are close in quality. All models are 2023-2024; no 2025-2026 model was measured in an opened source.
agent_test: Randomise candidate order, log position of the chosen candidate, and run a swapped re-check on near ties; compare position-chosen rate with uniform.

claim: Stop rules that need no answer key (consensus threshold, window agreement, trial-answer confidence, first-m-finished) cut tokens or samples by about 20 to 85% against a fixed-budget or full-chain baseline with accuracy mostly kept, on math, science QA and (DEER) code. No opened paper compares them at strictly equal tokens against a fixed-budget baseline; all are Pareto comparisons against longer baselines.
agent_test: Run stop-on-consensus vs fixed 3 and fixed 8 passes at matched total tokens on easy and hard items; report accuracy by difficulty bin.

claim: Answer-level stop signals fire too early on hard items: in PUMA, 42.4% of confidence-based and 54.8% of consistency-based stop failures were cases where the full chain would have reached the correct answer; Answer Convergence showed severe accuracy collapse; label-free stops are unstable on MATH-500 and GPQA (Liu and Wang). DeepConf notes overconfidence on wrong problems. This is the cost of a wrong stop on hard items.
agent_test: On hard items require a verifier pass or a second independent route before an early stop; compare with consensus-only stop.

claim: A cheap difficulty probe is learnable from hidden states (72 to 84% easy-vs-hard ranking accuracy; correctness probes reach ECE below 0.1 in distribution) but is domain-specific and degrades out of distribution (AIME, logic-to-math); question-text-only or prompt-only gating is unreliable. The best current choice for S0 is a pilot sample or partial attempt plus agreement, not a prompt-only guess (the pilot-vs-probe comparison itself was not found).
agent_test: Compare a one-sample pilot-agreement gate with a prompt-only gate on mixed easy and hard items; count hard items sent to the cheap path.

claim: No opened study varies candidate-set size (3 to 24) for an LLM selector, and no 2024-2026 paper testing adaptive aspiration levels (raise after success, lower after failure) in LLM agents was found. Search coverage was partial (web search quota exhausted, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex rate limited), so this is "not found", not "does not exist".
agent_test: Run the 3/6/12/24 set-size test and an adaptive-threshold variant ourselves at equal tokens.

claim: Shorter reasoning chains for the same question are up to 34.5% more accurate than the longest, and stopping at the first m of k parallel samples to finish (short-3@k) beats majority voting with up to 33% less wall time. Math and science QA only.
agent_test: Test first-finished-wins with m=3 against full majority vote at equal tokens.
